categories.main_business_segments: Chevron operates two primary business segments: Upstream and Downstream. The Upstream segment focuses on the exploration, development, production, and transportation of crude oil and natural gas, as well as liquefied natural gas (LNG) activities. The Downstream segment encompasses refining, marketing, and transportation of petroleum products, manufacturing and marketing of renewable fuels, petrochemicals, and fuel and lubricant additives. Additionally, Chevron has investments in chemicals (through Chevron Phillips Chemical Company) and new energies initiatives.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Chevron utilizes advanced exploration and production technologies, including horizontal drilling, hydraulic fracturing, deepwater development, and carbon capture and storage. The company employs factory development strategies in shale and tight oil plays, multi-well pad drilling, and integrated LNG processing. In refining, Chevron uses flexible, high-capacity refineries and is expanding renewable fuel production through biofuel refineries and co-processing renewable feedstocks. The company also invests in hydrogen, geothermal, and digital technologies, including artificial intelligence and advanced analytics.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Chevron serves a broad range of customers including industrial, commercial, and retail consumers. Key markets include transportation (fuels and lubricants), power generation (natural gas and LNG), petrochemical manufacturers, and commercial aviation (jet fuel). The company supplies products to branded service stations, commercial and industrial clients, and through joint ventures, also serves specialty chemical and plastics markets.
categories.geographic_coverage: Chevron has a global footprint with significant operations in North America (notably the U.S. Permian and DJ Basins, Gulf of Mexico), South America (Argentina, Brazil, Canada), Africa (Angola, Nigeria, Republic of Congo), Asia (Bangladesh, Israel, Kazakhstan, Thailand), Australia (Gorgon and Wheatstone LNG), and Europe (UK North Sea). The company’s activities span over 20 countries, with the U.S., Australia, and Kazakhstan representing major reserves and production centers.
categories.supply_chain_position: Chevron is an integrated energy company operating across the entire oil and gas value chain. It is active upstream (exploration and production), midstream (transportation, storage, and LNG), and downstream (refining, marketing, and chemicals). The company also participates in renewable energy production and carbon management, positioning itself from resource extraction to end-product delivery.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Chevron’s strategic focus is to deliver higher returns and lower carbon, aiming to lead in lower carbon intensity oil, products, and natural gas while expanding in renewable fuels, carbon capture, hydrogen, and emerging technologies. The company is investing approximately $10 billion through 2028 in lower carbon initiatives, including $2 billion to reduce the carbon intensity of its operations and $8 billion in new energy businesses. R&D efforts emphasize scalable, affordable energy solutions, digital transformation, and partnerships for innovation.
categories.revenue_model: Chevron generates revenue primarily through the sale of crude oil, natural gas, LNG, refined petroleum products, petrochemicals, and lubricants. Additional revenue streams include renewable fuels, specialty chemicals, and licensing of technology. The company also earns income from equity affiliates and joint ventures, as well as through trading and transportation services.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Chevron competes with major integrated oil and gas companies such as ExxonMobil, Shell, BP, and TotalEnergies, as well as national oil companies and independent producers. In refining and chemicals, it faces competition from both global majors and regional players. Chevron is positioned as one of the world’s largest publicly traded energy companies, with a strong presence in both traditional hydrocarbons and emerging lower-carbon businesses.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2023, Chevron reported $196.9 billion in sales and operating revenues and $21.4 billion in net income, with total assets of $261.6 billion. The company produced 3.1 million barrels of oil-equivalent per day, with a reserve base of 11.1 billion barrels of oil-equivalent. While 2023 saw a decline in earnings from 2022 due to lower commodity prices, Chevron maintains a robust balance sheet, strong free cash flow, and continues to invest in both core and new energy growth areas.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Chevron emphasizes reliable, affordable, and increasingly lower-carbon energy solutions, leveraging its scale, operational excellence, and technology leadership. The company differentiates itself through integrated operations, a diverse global asset base, a strong safety and environmental record, and a commitment to shareholder returns. Chevron’s growing investments in renewables, carbon management, and digital innovation further enhance its competitive positioning for the energy transition.
